faqs.a: We use Jest, Vitest, pytest, JUnit, NUnit, and xUnit for unit testing, combined with coverage tools like Istanbul, Coverage.py, and JaCoCo.

faqs.q: What is a good unit test coverage target?
faqs.a: We target 80% coverage as a baseline for production code, with 90%+ for critical business logic, payment processing, and safety-critical components.

faqs.q: How do you write tests for legacy codebases with no tests?
faqs.a: We start with characterisation tests to document existing behaviour, then refactor incrementally to improve testability while building coverage progressively.

faqs.q: Do you use TDD (Test-Driven Development)?
faqs.a: Yes. We advocate TDD for new feature development and can train your team on red-green-refactor cycles as part of the engagement.

faqs.q: How do you handle testing for third-party dependencies?
faqs.a: We use mocking and stubbing (Mockito, unittest.mock, Sinon) to isolate units from external dependencies, ensuring tests are fast and deterministic.

faqs.q: Can unit tests be integrated into our CI/CD pipeline?
faqs.a: Yes. We configure your pipeline to run the full unit test suite on every commit, with coverage gates that block merges below the agreed threshold.

faqs.q: What is the difference between RPA and intelligent automation?
faqs.a: RPA automates rule-based, structured tasks; intelligent automation adds AI capabilities like document understanding, NLP, and decision intelligence to handle unstructured data.

faqs.q: Which RPA platforms do you work with?
faqs.a: We develop on UiPath, Automation Anywhere, Microsoft Power Automate, and Blue Prism, selecting the platform that best fits your licensing, infrastructure, and IT governance requirements.

faqs.q: How do you identify the best processes to automate?
faqs.a: We conduct a process discovery workshop using task mining, interview sessions, and volume/complexity analysis to produce a prioritised automation opportunity pipeline.

faqs.q: How long does it take to automate a process?
faqs.a: Simple, well-documented processes can be automated in 2–4 weeks. Complex multi-system processes with exception handling typically take 6–10 weeks.

faqs.q: What happens when an automated process encounters an exception?
faqs.a: We design exception frameworks that route unhandled cases to human queues with full context, ensuring no transaction is lost and audit trails are maintained.

faqs.q: Do you provide ongoing bot maintenance?
faqs.a: Yes. Our managed automation services include bot monitoring, application change remediation, performance reporting, and continuous improvement recommendations.

faqs.q: What BPM platforms do you implement?
faqs.a: We implement Pega, Appian, IBM BPM, SAP Signavio, and Camunda, as well as building custom BPM solutions on modern workflow engines where appropriate.

faqs.q: How do you model and document our current processes?
faqs.a: We use BPMN 2.0 notation in tools such as Signavio or Lucidchart, facilitated through process discovery workshops with process owners and subject matter experts.

faqs.q: What is process mining and do we need it?
faqs.a: Process mining uses system event logs to discover the actual execution paths of your processes, revealing deviations, bottlenecks, and rework loops invisible to manual analysis.

faqs.q: How long does a BPM implementation take?
faqs.a: Single process automation implementations run 6–10 weeks. Enterprise-wide BPM programmes with multiple processes and integrations typically take 6–18 months.

faqs.q: Can BPM solutions integrate with our existing ERP?
faqs.a: Yes. We build native integrations with SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, and other enterprise platforms so BPM orchestrates workflows across your full technology landscape.

faqs.q: How do you ensure process governance after go-live?
faqs.a: We implement process ownership frameworks, KPI dashboards, SLA monitoring, and regular process review cadences to ensure continuous improvement post-deployment.
